data.gender_notes: Bisharat is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bisharat is an Arabic name for boys that means swiftness, grace, and success. It is a name that conveys the idea of being quick and efficient in one's actions, as well as being elegant and refined in one's demeanor. The name is derived from the Arabic root word 'sh-r-t', which means 'to be swift' or 'to go quickly'. It is a name that is often given to boys who are expected to excel in their endeavors and to make a positive impact in the world.

It reflects the idea that one should move through life with ease and grace, overcoming obstacles and challenges with speed and agility. It is a name that inspires one to be quick in thought and action, and to be guided by a deep sense of inner wisdom and intuition. It is also a name that resonates with the spiritual principle of 'tawakkul', or trust in God, as it reminds us that success and victory come from divine guidance and support.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab al-Tabaqat al-Kabir, vol. 1, p. 122. Bishr ibn Marwan was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad who later became the commander of the Muslim army during the Battle of Mu'tah in 629 AD against the Byzantine and Ghassanid forces. His nickname was 'Bishr al-Bishr' (Bishr the Generous) or 'Bishr al-Khafaji' (Bishr the Swift) due to his bravery and generosity during the battle. However, he is more commonly known as Bishr ibn Marwan al-Bishri.
historical_references.context: Battle of Mu'tah against Byzantine and Ghassanid forces

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr, p. 113. Bishr ibn Marwan is also mentioned as one of the commanders of the Muslim expedition to Egypt in 640 AD led by 'Amr ibn al-As.
